title: Parkinson’s connectivity retrieval found similarly mixed neighbors for cases and controls
summary: Among 40 participants in the TaoWu cohort, the ten closest matches in a learned connectivity representation were 79.5% Parkinson’s cases for diagnosed participants and 81.0% for controls, on average. The source pool included 139 people with Parkinson’s among 169 participants. Retrieval did not consistently improve classification beyond pretraining alone.
organization: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg

source_review.scope: v1 cohort Methods, Table 1 and Figure 2 controls; PDF author affiliation

evidence.tested: A frozen encoder was trained on external cohorts. The researchers summarized matched neighbor labels and compared prediction variants using repeated cross-validation in the separate TaoWu cohort.
evidence.unknown: The study is small and the source lookup is label-imbalanced. Same-fold checkpoint selection and cohort differences limit interpretation of classification metrics.
evidence.ai_role: A graph convolutional autoencoder learned functional-connectivity embeddings from 169 external individuals. Neighbor identities and a downstream classifier evaluated a separate 40-person sample.
